submission.justification: Simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c: R3 peaks near 2 cm (4.60 sigma; 4.52 at 4 cm, 4.37 at 3 cm, 3.49 at 6 cm). R2 is 3.65 sigma at 2 cm (3.63 at 4 cm, 3.91 at 3 cm, 2.66 at 6 cm). R1 is 2.76 sigma at 3 cm and 2.05 at 6 cm. R3 gives the best separation, but it is an untreated high-index porous radiator. R2 is the porous option with a hydrophobic treatment, which is the mitigation most relevant to the humidity-ageing hard constraint. I chose R2 at 2 cm as the option most likely to satisfy the constraint, at a cost of about 0.95 sigma against R3. The project documents contain no humidity-ageing or transparency-loss data for any candidate, and the simulation tool does not report transparency. So compliance with the 10% transparency-loss limit is UNVERIFIED for R2 and for R3. Before procurement, the 10-year humidity ageing test must be run on the chosen radiator. If R2 fails it, the fallback is R1, the solid radiator, but it has the lowest separation. R3 should be chosen only if its ageing test passes.

requirements.evidence: R2 at 2 cm gives 3.65 sigma, below R3 at 2 cm (4.60 sigma). R2 was chosen for humidity robustness, which trades away separation. This is a deliberate trade-off, not the maximum separation.
